default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1508.title: Gap-side box-break fade
E-1508.hypothesis: After an opening gap the overnight side is already positioned and gap traders hold the move; a short box break further in the gap's direction is late chasing that finds the gap holders taking profit, so it fades, while breaks against the gap are left alone.

E-1509.title: Spiky-volume day box-break fade
E-1509.hypothesis: When the session's volume so far is concentrated in a few bars (high Herfindahl share versus the usual at this minute), the day's real flow arrived in bursts and the tape between bursts is liquidity providers quoting a thin book; a short box break between bursts has no initiator behind it and reverts.

E-1510.title: FX-driven day index box-break fade
E-1510.hypothesis: When the dollar's range so far is large next to the index's range (versus the usual ratio at this minute), the day's information is in FX and index moves are hedge and arbitrage legs that mean-revert around the dollar; a short WIN box break on such a day has no equity initiator, so fade it.

E-1511.title: Exit-scale wide box break fade
E-1511.hypothesis: A box whose width is several times the fixed 150-point exit is a rotation with defended edges far apart; a close beyond one edge meets the resting orders of the box's range traders and the fade target lies well inside the box, so a modest rotation back is enough; fade the break.

E-1512.title: Light opening-auction day box-break fade
E-1512.hypothesis: A small opening-auction print (versus the 20 previous sessions) means no overnight imbalance had to be matched: institutions came in without urgency and the day is left to intraday liquidity providers; short box breaks on such days lack initiative and rotate back.

E-1513.title: Box value-skew break trade
E-1513.hypothesis: Where the box's volume traded (its VWAP position inside the box) shows which prices were accepted; a break toward the accepted side is continuation of value, a break away from it is a probe the volume will not support; on any break, trade toward the side where the box's volume sits.

E-1514.title: Multi-day close-stretch box-break fade
E-1514.hypothesis: When price sits more than k standard deviations away from the mean of the last ten session closes, swing traders and multi-day mean-reversion desks are leaning against the stretch; a short box break that extends the stretch meets their orders and fades.

E-1515.title: Lunch-box break fade
E-1515.hypothesis: The midday hour's range on B3 is set in thin trade; screened breakouts of this box lose clearly when followed, because the afternoon first probes it with stop orders that liquidity providers absorb before the US flow sets the real direction; fade the first close beyond the lunch box.

E-1516.title: One-bar box traverse fade
E-1516.hypothesis: A single bar that covers a large share of the recent box and closes beyond it is one aggressive order sweeping the book through every resting level; the sweeper is done once filled and the swept liquidity providers refill behind it, so the break gives part back; fade it.

E-1517.title: Post-spike aftershock break fade
E-1517.hypothesis: In the minutes after a bar with abnormal volume for its time (news or block execution), the market digests the spike and liquidity providers re-quote wide; small box breaks during the cooldown are aftershocks from late reactors, not new information, so fade them.
